meta.title: Ransomware — The Gentlemen (RMM supply-chain intrusion)
meta.systems: RMM-AGENT (managed endpoints), WKS-FIN07 (finance workstation, entry), DC-CORP01 (domain controller), FS-SHARE01 (file server), HV-CLUSTER01 (Hyper-V host), BKP-VEEAM01 (backup server), WKS-HR03 (HR workstation)
meta.containment: Isolated all endpoints managed by the compromised RMM tenant; suspended the MSP RMM integration and revoked its API token; blocked the malicious GPO and forced gpupdate reversal domain-wide; removed ThrottleBlood.sys / All.exe / Allpatch2.exe and the AnyDesk unattended install; disabled attacker service accounts; reset all privileged credentials and double-reset krbtgt; isolated Hyper-V and backup servers before encryption reached them.
meta.narrative:
Between 19 and 28 August 2026 The Gentlemen ransomware operation gained and expanded access to the corporate environment, culminating in an attempt to deploy ransomware domain-wide. The intrusion is notable for its initial access vector: rather than phishing or an exposed VPN, the actor abused the organisation's managed service provider (MSP) remote monitoring and management (RMM) tooling.

On 19 August a valid but stolen MSP technician credential was used to authenticate to the RMM platform and push a scripted 'maintenance' task to a finance workstation (WKS-FIN07). Because the RMM agent is a trusted, allow-listed management tool, the initial payload ran without triggering application-control or raising analyst suspicion — the activity looked like routine managed IT. This supply-chain-adjacent entry is the novel element of the case and the reason dwell time reached nine days before detection.

From that foothold the actor conducted discovery, harvested credentials and moved laterally with legitimate administrative utilities — PsExec and PuTTY for movement, PowerRun.exe for a UAC bypass to SYSTEM. Defence evasion followed The Gentlemen's documented playbook: a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver technique using ThrottleBlood.sys (a renamed ThrottleStop.sys driver, exploiting CVE-2025-7771) loaded via All.exe to terminate protected EDR processes at the kernel level, with Allpatch2.exe generating an environment-specific bypass for the endpoint suite in use. The actor then abused a Group Policy Object to stage the locker for domain-wide execution, and established redundant persistence via an AnyDesk unattended install and modified registry run keys.

Approximately 45GB of finance and HR data was exfiltrated over an encrypted WinSCP channel before encryption. Detection came on 28 August when the EDR platform alerted on tampering as the driver attempted to terminate its protected service on the Hyper-V host — the one endpoint where the tailored bypass failed. Rapid isolation prevented the GPO-staged locker from executing across the domain: encryption was limited to WKS-FIN07 and FS-SHARE01, and the Hyper-V cluster and Veeam backup server were isolated intact, enabling clean recovery. Containment completed 29 August; eradication, credential rotation and recovery finished 02 September. The MSP relationship and RMM tenant security were the primary post-incident focus.

govern.assets: RMM tenant, WKS-FIN07, DC-CORP01, FS-SHARE01, HV-CLUSTER01, BKP-VEEAM01, WKS-HR03
govern.dataTypes: Finance records, HR/employee PII, payroll data
govern.legalNotes: Reportable to ICO (employee PII in exfiltrated set). MSP contract and liability under legal review given the compromise originated via their RMM access. Privilege asserted over technical report.
govern.secureComms: Signal bridge — corporate email trusted (not implicated) but used out of caution until 29 Aug
govern.bizImpact: Two endpoints and one file server encrypted; recovered from isolated Veeam backups within 3 days. No domain-wide encryption — GPO-staged locker was blocked before execution. Estimated direct response cost £220k-£300k including external IR, MSP transition and overtime. ~4 day partial disruption to finance operations.
govern.repRisk: Medium-high — MSP supply-chain origin and Gentlemen leak-site listing threatened; data published assessed unlikely after negotiation lapsed without payment. Controlled disclosure to affected staff only.
govern.insurance: Cyber policy CYB-88213 (Beazley). Claim CLM-2026-0828 opened 29 Aug. Excess £75k. MSP's own liability being pursued separately.
govern.riskNotes: Primary residual risk was re-entry via the MSP RMM channel; integration suspended and rebuilt on a new tenant with scoped, MFA-enforced, time-boxed access. Threat-hunt all-clear 02 Sep.

iocs.notes: Stolen MSP technician account used to authenticate to the RMM console. Valid credential; origin traced to the MSP, not the client. Novel entry vector.
Gentlemen affiliate infrastructure / leak-site-adjacent domain identified during enrichment.
Malicious scripted task pushed via the trusted RMM agent to WKS-FIN07. Allow-listed management tool, so the payload ran without application-control friction. This is the initial-access mechanism.
Source the RMM task beaconed to on execution — actor infrastructure behind the RMM channel.
Encoded PowerShell loader delivered by the RMM task; staged the toolkit into %USERPROFILE%\Downloads.
Domain and privileged-group enumeration two days after access — deliberate, low-noise discovery.
SHA-256 of an LSASS dump artefact. Credentials harvested for lateral movement.
Compromised privileged service account whose credentials enabled movement to backup and virtualisation hosts.
PsExec used to move laterally and transfer tooling — a documented Gentlemen lateral-movement utility.
PowerRun.exe used for UAC bypass and escalation to SYSTEM — Gentlemen-associated tooling.
Internal source of SMB lateral movement to the file server.
Renamed ThrottleStop.sys driver (CVE-2025-7771) loaded to gain kernel execution and kill protected EDR processes. BYOVD — The Gentlemen's signature technique. Recovered from %USERPROFILE%\Downloads.
SHA-256 of the ThrottleBlood.sys driver. Shared with NCSC and Mandiant.
Gentlemen EDR-killer that invokes the vulnerable driver to terminate protected security services.
Custom Gentlemen anti-security utility that live-profiles the EDR in use and generates a tailored bypass. Failed on the Hyper-V host, which triggered detection.
AnyDesk silently installed for unattended access with a preset password and updates disabled — redundant persistence per Gentlemen tradecraft.
Registry Run key persistence, second redundant mechanism.
Malicious Group Policy Object modification staging the ransomware locker as an immediate scheduled task for domain-wide execution. Blocked before it ran. Gentlemen signature technique.
C2 domain used by the staged toolkit. Low-frequency HTTPS beaconing. Sinkholed at containment.
IPv6 C2 endpoint seen late in the intrusion. Added to egress block.
WinSCP used for encrypted exfiltration of ~45GB finance and HR data prior to encryption — documented Gentlemen exfil channel.
Destination endpoint receiving the WinSCP-exfiltrated archive over encrypted transport.
Data-transfer-size anomaly across three SFTP sessions totalling ~45GB, in the exfiltration window before encryption.
Gentlemen ransom note dropped in encrypted directories on the two hosts reached before containment. References Tox contact and leak site.
Extension appended to encrypted files. Encryption limited to WKS-FIN07 and FS-SHARE01; domain-wide GPO execution was blocked.
Shadow-copy deletion immediately before encryption to inhibit local recovery.

actions.title: Isolate all RMM-managed endpoints; suspend RMM integration
actions.notes: All managed endpoints isolated; MSP RMM API token revoked.

actions.title: Block malicious GPO and force domain-wide reversal
actions.notes: Locker-staging GPO removed; gpupdate /force pushed; verified via gpresult.

actions.title: Remove BYOVD toolkit + AnyDesk + registry persistence
actions.notes: ThrottleBlood.sys, All.exe, Allpatch2.exe, AnyDesk, Run key removed across affected hosts.

actions.title: Rotate all credentials; double-reset krbtgt
actions.notes: All privileged + service accounts rotated; krbtgt reset twice with replication interval.

actions.title: Verify + isolate Veeam backups before recovery
actions.notes: BKP-VEEAM01 confirmed unencrypted and isolated; integrity verified before restore.

actions.title: Assess exfiltration scope (WinSCP channel)
actions.notes: ~45GB: finance records, HR/employee PII, payroll. Informed ICO decision.

actions.title: Recover encrypted hosts from backup
actions.notes: WKS-FIN07 and FS-SHARE01 rebuilt and restored from isolated Veeam backups.

actions.title: Rebuild RMM on new tenant with scoped MFA access
actions.notes: New RMM tenant; MSP access scoped, MFA-enforced, time-boxed, session-logged.

actions.title: Estate-wide EDR sensor version audit
actions.notes: Hosts on older sensor build identified and upgraded — the version gap let the driver kill EDR on some hosts.

escalations.reason: BYOVD EDR-kill, domain-wide GPO locker staging and active encryption elevate to critical. Potential full-domain ransomware.
Held at critical through eradication despite containment, pending backup-integrity confirmation and threat-hunt all-clear.

notifications.notes: Reported; Gentlemen IOCs shared via MISP.
Employee PII in exfiltrated set; reported within 72h. Ref ICO-2026-31xxxx.
Board briefed at detection; twice-daily thereafter.
Engaged for privilege, regulatory strategy and MSP contract/liability review.

notifications.basis: Compromise originated via MSP RMM access
notifications.notes: Formal notice served on the MSP; their credential compromise was the entry vector. Liability under review.
Staff whose PII was in the exfiltrated set notified with guidance, on DPO advice.

rootCauses.detail: The MSP's RMM technician account had standing, always-on access to the entire estate with no MFA and no session time-boxing. A single stolen MSP credential gave the actor trusted, allow-listed execution on any managed endpoint — the initial-access vector.
rootCauses.remediation: RMM rebuilt on a new tenant with scoped, MFA-enforced, time-boxed, session-logged access. MSP access now least-privilege and reviewed quarterly; contract updated with security obligations.

rootCauses.factor: RMM agent implicitly trusted by application control
rootCauses.detail: Because the RMM agent is a legitimate management tool, its scripted tasks bypassed application-control and did not raise analyst suspicion, enabling the initial payload to run unimpeded.
rootCauses.remediation: RMM task execution now monitored and alerted; script-block logging enabled; unexpected RMM-spawned PowerShell flagged in the SIEM.

rootCauses.factor: Inconsistent EDR sensor versions across the estate
rootCauses.detail: Some hosts ran an older EDR sensor build vulnerable to the BYOVD kill; the driver terminated protection on those hosts. Detection only occurred because a newer build on the Hyper-V host resisted the tailored bypass.
rootCauses.remediation: Estate-wide sensor version standardised and auto-update enforced; vulnerable-driver blocklist (including ThrottleStop/ThrottleBlood) deployed.

rootCauses.detail: The malicious Default Domain Policy change that staged the domain-wide locker went unalerted; only rapid containment stopped it applying.
rootCauses.remediation: GPO change auditing and real-time alerting enabled on all domain policies; SYSVOL scheduled-task changes flagged.

hostAnalysis.summary: Confirmed point of entry. The RMM agent executed a malicious 'Finance PC Maintenance' task at 08:52 on 19 Aug, delivering an encoded PowerShell loader that staged the Gentlemen toolkit to the Downloads folder. LSASS was dumped on 21 Aug and PowerRun.exe used for UAC bypass to SYSTEM. This host was one of two encrypted before containment; the ransom note and .gentlemen extension are present.
hostAnalysis.notes: Timeline reconstructed from EDR process tree + prefetch. RMM task ID in the platform log = TASK-88213. Loader was AMSI-bypassed — check whether AMSI bypass signature matches known Gentlemen loader. Downloads folder had All.exe, Allpatch2.exe, PowerRun.exe. TODO: confirm exact PowerShell decode offline (done — see IOC g05).

hostAnalysis.summary: The detection trigger. On 27 Aug the actor attempted to load ThrottleBlood.sys (renamed ThrottleStop.sys, CVE-2025-7771) via All.exe to terminate the protected EDR service at kernel level. The tailored Allpatch2 bypass failed on this host's EDR build, and the tamper attempt raised the alert that surfaced the whole intrusion. No encryption reached the Hyper-V cluster; it was isolated intact.
hostAnalysis.notes: Driver recovered from C:\Users\svc-backup-adm\Downloads. Confirmed Authenticode signature on the driver (legitimately signed ThrottleStop) — that's why it loaded. EDR held here because of a newer sensor build; other hosts were on the older build. Recommend estate-wide sensor version audit.

hostAnalysis.summary: Domain-wide staging point. The actor modified the Default Domain Policy GPO on 27 Aug to register the ransomware locker as an immediate scheduled task, intending domain-wide execution. This was blocked during containment before the policy applied broadly. A registry Run-key persistence entry was also set here. krbtgt was double-reset during recovery.
hostAnalysis.notes: GPO change found in SYSVOL ScheduledTasks.xml — timestamp 20:15 27 Aug, ~5h before we contained. If detection had been slower this would have encrypted the whole domain. The GPO edit was made with svc-backup-adm. Pulled gpresult from 6 hosts to confirm the policy hadn't applied. Verified clean post-reversal.

hostAnalysis.summary: Root of the intrusion. Audit logs, obtained with MSP cooperation, show authentication with a valid technician credential (msp-tech-svc7) at 08:41 on 19 Aug from an anomalous source, immediately followed by the scripted task push to WKS-FIN07. The credential compromise originated at the MSP, not the client. The RMM integration has been suspended and rebuilt on a new tenant with scoped, MFA-enforced, time-boxed access.
hostAnalysis.notes: MSP initially slow to provide logs — escalated via legal. Their account msp-tech-svc7 had standing access to our whole estate with no MFA and no session time-box. This is the crux of the case for the lessons-learned and the MSP contract review. No evidence the MSP was itself ransomed — looks like a targeted credential theft against them.

hostAnalysis.summary: Corroborated C2 and exfiltration. Netflow shows ~45GB outbound over three SFTP (WinSCP) sessions in the early hours of 27 Aug, immediately before encryption, to 203.0.113.99. Low-frequency HTTPS beaconing to update-cdn-sync[.]net runs across the dwell period from 20 Aug.
hostAnalysis.notes: Still cross-referencing full beacon cadence — want to confirm first beacon time precisely for the timeline. Exfil volume (45GB) matches the finance+HR share size roughly. IPv6 C2 only appeared from 25 Aug. Netflow retention only 30 days — exported before rollover.

closure.notes: All containment, eradication, evidence, IOC-sharing, recovery and notification steps complete. Domain-wide encryption prevented — locker staging blocked before execution. Backups verified and hosts restored. RMM rebuilt securely. Threat-hunt all-clear 02 Sep. Closed by IR lead with CISO sign-off.

lessons.attendees: Dan H, Priya S, Marcus O, Helena Marsh (CISO), Eleanor Voss (Legal), Raj Patel (DPO), Mandiant lead
lessons.well: Detection, though late, caught the intrusion before domain-wide encryption — the newer EDR build on the Hyper-V host held against the tailored bypass and raised the tamper alert. Backups were isolated and verified before any restore, enabling clean recovery with no ransom paid. Out-of-band comms and counsel were engaged immediately.
lessons.better: Nine days' dwell was too long. The MSP RMM channel was a blind spot — over-privileged, no MFA, unmonitored — and is the single biggest failure. EDR sensor versions were inconsistent, which is why the driver kill succeeded on some hosts. GPO changes were unmonitored.
lessons.detect: Alert on RMM-spawned PowerShell and unexpected RMM task execution. Enable GPO-modification and SYSVOL scheduled-task alerting. Deploy a vulnerable-driver blocklist and alert on ThrottleStop/ThrottleBlood-class driver loads. Add outbound SFTP/WinSCP volume anomaly alerting.
lessons.playbook: Add a 'third-party/MSP RMM compromise' playbook: how to suspend an integration, revoke tokens and isolate managed endpoints fast. Add a BYOVD response checklist. Pre-authorise MSP log requests via contract to avoid the delay we hit.
lessons.training: Brief analysts on RMM-abuse indicators and BYOVD tradecraft. Tabletop an MSP-origin intrusion. Workshop GPO-integrity monitoring with the AD team.
lessons.recs: 1) Re-scope all third-party/MSP access to least-privilege, MFA-enforced, time-boxed and logged. 2) Standardise EDR sensor versions estate-wide and enforce a vulnerable-driver blocklist. 3) Enable GPO and SYSVOL change alerting. 4) Monitor and alert on RMM task execution. 5) Bake MSP security obligations and log-access SLAs into the contract.
